commenti.body: I like learning about what makes people do the things the do, how they become the way they are, why they succeed and fail. Character studies, the effects of intangible forces on tangible reality, life.
To be entertained.
No not really. I can't back that up.
they're a distraction from the harsh reality because life sucks

Because I truly love the art form.

I appreciate certain films because they are mindlessly entertaining but I also appreciate other kinds of films that offer some insight on the human condition, or are experimental, express unique views or further the art form in some way.

There are many different reasons depending on what type of film I'm watching, but the common reason is love and respect for the art form, which is probably one of the most important and influential forms of art of the last 100 years or so.

To get out of my own head, to get a new perspective, to travel without traveling. Also I think to try to understand speaking better, I don’t always have a ton of social interaction, or only have it between a limited number of people, so sometimes movies and podcasts go a long way for getting the feel of conversation.

In other cases, like with horror, I think to get that immersive and narrowing feeling that being freaked out gives you, it’s hard to worry about random bs when you’re sufficiently in the mood of a good horror movie

Entertainment. Why?
Because I'm bored and lazy.
A vacation for the mind, a playground for the imagination.

It’s my own little personal cocoon of which I have the power to invite people in or do it myself. There are many go to movies of where I can just forget about anything else in life for a couple hours but I will say that the one movie that never fails me for that is Harry Potter 1.

So many reasons, I guess.

I like the visual aspect. I love beautiful camera shots, the cameras motion.

I like the emotional response movies makes in me. They can make me laugh, cry.

I like the thougts they start in my brain. I wonder about what the director wants, how I interpret what I see, symbols, meanings, all of that.

And finally I am interested in the history of movies. How it evolved from the early days. How different genres came by, who made them first, who inspired who. I like reading about it, I like reading books by directors.
I'm just a slave to the system so when I can keep my simple monkey brain entertained it's one of the best forms of background noise for me

Why do you watch movies?

I used to watch them because when my wife and I were first dating, she always wanted to see the new movies coming out. Our first date was seeing the continuation of The Thing. We soon began to find genres that we both enjoy. She has gotten more into the action/comedy movies, and I have gotten more into horror/suspense. From that point on, I went from a watcher to a fanatic. We still watch movies together to this day.

I like being told stories. If it's in a visual medium then it pleases me. 

Pretty simple I suppose ; )

I look at movies like literature. There are layers in every element of cinema that gets expanded on. Directors grow and find there style as does actors and musical composers. It all attracts me and the decision they make to bring emphasis on certain subjects and scenarios. I watch to escape, to be entertaining, to discover, and to listen to stories out of my comfort zone.
